label: first copy step (re-reading orig token 0) in long sequences, favoring first tokens t/u/c/o/0 and second tokens j/u/t/g/2/i
explanation: Almost all activity (89% of mass) is at recall_idx==1, the first copy step right after <DEL>, where the input is the fed-back original token 0 and the output is original token 1. A small amount appears on the <DEL> step itself (2%), and there is essentially nothing in the original phase. Within that step it strongly prefers long sequences (L=9 holds 70% of mass, L=8 23%, almost none for L<=6) and specific identities: first token t/u/c/o/0 and second token j/u/t/g/2/i. The strongest activations (about 0.9-1.0 of max) are on pairs like t->u, o->t, c->j, t->j, 0->j. Even with all three conditions, precision is only about 14%, so it also depends on the rest of the sequence content in a way I could not capture with simple token-presence sets. It does not fire at later copy steps, and it does not fire on short sequences.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues.
